input: This passage describes the duty point of a centrifugal pump that is used to move caustic solution between two vessels that are located at grade. At the duty point, the pump delivers a flow of 64 m3 h-1 against a head of 33 m, and it operates with an efficiency of 67%. Under these conditions, the shaft power required at the duty point is 8.6 kW. In order to provide a suitable margin for the drive, the motor that powers the pump is rated 15% above this value. During the acceptance test that was carried out on the pump, no cavitation was observed, although it is important to note that this test ran for 4 h at the duty point only. This means that the absence of cavitation has been demonstrated at the tested condition, while behaviour at other flows and at other points on the operating curve has not been covered by the test at all. Some care is therefore needed when drawing broader conclusions about the performance of the pump across its full operating range, since a machine that runs quietly at its duty point may behave quite differently when it is asked to operate well away from that point, where the flow through the pump and the conditions at the suction side are no longer those that were examined during acceptance.
target: A centrifugal pump moves caustic solution between two vessels at grade. At the duty point the flow is 64 m3 h-1 against a head of 33 m, with pump efficiency 67%. Shaft power at the duty point is 8.6 kW, and the motor is rated 15% above this value. The duty point is the condition the pump was selected for, and the figures belong to that condition as a set: flow, head, and efficiency are the values the pump delivers there, and the shaft power follows from them. Cavitation was not observed in the acceptance test. The test ran for 4 h at the duty point only, so the result is a detection statement for that condition and no other: no cavitation at the duty point over the duration of the test. Behaviour at other flows is untested. Away from the duty point the suction conditions change with flow, and the absence of cavitation at the tested point does not extend along the pump curve in either direction; a statement about cavitation at higher or lower flow needs a test at that flow. The margin on the motor belongs to the same discipline: the drive is sized above the duty-point shaft power so that the machine can deliver the duty without running at its limit, and the margin is stated against the duty point because that is the condition the selection was made for. None of the figures describes the pump at part load or at overload, and an enquiry about either condition starts from the pump curve and the system the pump works against, not from the duty-point set.
